findings.reason: from_events.ts:229-241 adds documents to state.stream only on EVENT_POP and now returns state.stream with no frames.length check. eventsToAst and createParserState are exported (index.ts:185-193), so events [DOCUMENT] or [DOCUMENT, SCALAR] return []. The constructor path still checks this (constructor.ts:456). I lowered C1 from high to medium because the trigger needs a hand-built or partly filled ParserState; normal parseEvents output is balanced.
findings.claim: Removing the end-of-stream frames check makes the exported eventsToAst silently drop unfinished documents and return a truncated or empty Stream.
findings.evidence: The diff deletes `if (state.frames.length !== 0) throwErrorAt(parserState, state.position, 'unexpected end of event stream')` before `return state.stream`. A document is only added in `case EVENT_POP` (`state.stream.push(frame.doc)`). Trigger: a ParserState whose events are [DOCUMENT, SCALAR] with no POP (built with the exported `createParserState`, or left partly filled after `parseEvents` threw and the caller caught the error). The loop ends with frames=[document] and returns `[]`. Nothing else guards this: the matching check survives only in `constructEvents` (src/parser/constructor.ts:456), which is a separate code path.

findings.reason: from_events.ts:230 uses `state.frames.pop()!` and addNode at :153-155 reads frame.kind with no guard, so [POP] or [SCALAR] throws TypeError reading 'kind' of undefined. constructor.ts:321 and :439 still throw positioned errors for the same input.
findings.claim: Removing the frame guards turns malformed event streams (an extra POP, or a node before any DOCUMENT) into untyped TypeErrors with no position, where they used to raise YAMLException.
findings.evidence: In `addNode` the diff removes `if (!frame) throwErrorAt(state.parserState, state.position, 'node appears outside a document')`, so `frame.kind` is read from `undefined` when the events start with SCALAR or ALIAS before DOCUMENT. In `case EVENT_POP`, `const frame = state.frames.pop()!` replaces the `unexpected collection end` check, so an extra POP causes `frame.kind` to throw a TypeError. The parallel constructor path still raises these errors with `throwError` (constructor.ts:321, 439), so the two public entry points now behave differently on the same bad input.

findings.reason: A grep for the three error messages finds them only in src/parser/constructor.ts. No test exercises them on the eventsToAst path, and the diff contains only removals plus the import cleanup.
findings.claim: The validation checks are deleted with no stated reason, and no test covers malformed event streams for eventsToAst, so the suite cannot catch the regression.
findings.evidence: The whole diff consists of removed checks and the now-unused `throwErrorAt` import. The tests that call `eventsToAst` (test/spec/spec.test.mjs:330, test/core/ast/presenter.test.mjs:20) only feed it well-formed `parseEvents` output. No test in the repository references 'node appears outside a document', 'unexpected collection end' or 'unexpected end of event stream' for this path.
